24 rigged, animated gym exercises as drop-in .glb files — squat, deadlift, push-up, plank and 20 more. Works in Three.js, Unity, Godot, Unreal, or a plain model-viewer tag. Includes a muscle-group manifest and form-cue steps for every exercise. MIT licensed — ship it in your commercial app.

--- START ---
See all 24 animations running live before you buy: https://assiamahs.github.io/opengym3d/

Building a fitness app, workout game, or exercise site? Skip weeks of 3D work.

This pack gives you 24 looping exercise animations — one .glb per exercise — each with a matching PNG thumbnail and a JSON manifest carrying the name, equipment, difficulty, primary and secondary muscle groups, and step-by-step form cues for the movement. That means it powers your exercise cards, tooltips, and coaching UI, not just the visuals.

WHAT YOU GET

- 24 animated .glb files (glTF binary), one looping clip baked into each file
- 24 matching 512x512 PNG thumbnails, muscle groups highlighted
- 24 pose-definition JSONs, so you can retarget or retime any movement
- exercises.json master manifest: name, equipment, difficulty, primary/secondary muscles, step-by-step form cues
- MIT LICENSE file included in the download
- About 2.7 MB per model, 43 MB total

THE 24 EXERCISES

Bent-Over Row, Bicep Curl, Calf Raise, Crunch, Deadlift, Dumbbell Shoulder Press, Front Raise, Glute Bridge, Good Morning, Hammer Curl, High Knees, Jumping Jack, Lateral Raise, Lunge, Overhead Press, Overhead Tricep Extension, Plank, Push-Up, Reverse Lunge, Romanian Deadlift, Squat, Sumo Squat, Superman, Wall Sit.

WORKS EVERYWHERE glTF WORKS

Three.js and React Three Fiber, Babylon.js, Unity (via glTFast or UnityGLTF), Godot 4, Unreal Engine's glTF importer, or a plain <model-viewer> tag on any web page. No proprietary format, no plugin to buy.

SIX LINES TO A PLAYING ANIMATION (Three.js)

import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
const gltf = await new GLTFLoader().loadAsync('models/squat.glb');
scene.add(gltf.scene);
const mixer = new THREE.AnimationMixer(gltf.scene);
mixer.clipAction(gltf.animations[0]).play();
// call mixer.update(delta) in your render loop

LICENSE

MIT. Use it in commercial apps, games, and websites. No attribution required, though it is always appreciated. Figure generated with MPFB2; animations authored from the pose definitions included in the pack.

Instant download, single zip, no account or subscription needed.
--- END ---
